definition: Variegated means marked with patches of different colors; diversified.
task: Write one sentence of your own using the word variegated. Make the sentence show what the word means -- a reader who did not know variegated should be able to work it out from your sentence.
avoid_verbatim: The koi pond's celebrity is a variegated carp, its back a drifting map of orange, white, and ink black.
Two-tone allows exactly two colors in orderly blocks, well short of variegated.
Speckled goes further than two-tone, scattering flecks of another color about, but it stops short of variegated, whose surface breaks into whole patches of several colors.

Mottled means blotched irregularly, usually in two muddled shades that smear into each other — camouflage, or the back of an old mirror. Variegated keeps its colors distinct: separate patches, each holding its own hue, mapped across one surface. Mottled blurs the boundaries; variegated draws them.

Dappled means spotted with soft patches of light and shade — sun through leaves onto a path — and it shifts as the light shifts. Variegated is about pigment, not illumination: patches of genuinely different colors fixed in the surface itself, like a leaf edged in cream.

The weaver's prize yarn is variegated, dyed so that a single strand slides from teal through copper to cream every arm's length.
Knitted up, no two rows of the scarf repeat, and buyers at her stall keep turning the finished pieces over, hunting for a pattern that was never there.

Variegated is more exact than 'colorful' because it describes how the color sits: in distinct patches or zones of different colors across one surface — a leaf edged in cream, a hillside quilted by autumn.
Colorful only promises brightness; variegated promises a map.
Gardeners use it almost technically, for leaves carrying two or more colors at once.
Variegated is the precision tool of gardeners, geologists, and catalog writers: it says the colors sit in distinct patches on one surface.
Mottled blurs the patches into blotches; dappled scatters soft spots of light.
Figuratively it can mean diversified — a variegated career — but in this unit protean owns change over time; variegated is variety you can see all at once.

From the fire tower in October, Ranger Beatriz maps the ridge by color.
The forest below is variegated: a patch of birch gold here, a block of maple red beside it, wedges of spruce holding their dark green between them.
Each stand keeps to its own patch, so the boundaries between colors are sharp enough to trace with a pencil.
Her survey partner jokes that the ridge looks like a stained-glass window laid on its back.
The colors are in the trees themselves, Beatriz notes — the map she draws at noon still matches the ridge at dusk.
